suited by today's longer trip.[Chris Wilson]

Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR
Talk To The Man 6 11-6 P Nicholls Harry Cobden 11-8 - 116 138
Paul Nicholls has won three of the last five runnings of this race; this Irish point winner (good to
yielding) left his bumper form behind when comfortably accounting for his penalised market
rival in a 2m3f novice at Taunton (heavy); it's difficult to know how good he might be and he
commands considerable respect.
The Big Clubman 6 11-6 P Nolan (IRE) Sean O'Keeffe 5-6 132 125 136
Irish challenger with an Albert Bartlett entry at Cheltenham; won maiden at Wexford on good
ground and stayed on well from off pace to be second in a 2m4f Grade 3 at Navan (heavy);
latest run in a Grade 2 wasn't so clever, but that was over 2m7f and it turned into a sprint finish;
nice prospect.
Agent Argylle 6 11-0 R Phillips Finn Lambert (3) 100-1 - 94 98
Irish point winner; shaped okay behind a smart winner in a bumper at Wetherby but still went off
at 80-1 for hurdle debut at Doncaster and ended up tailed off.
Big Bert 6 11-0 J Owen Sean Bowen 16-1 - 63 107
Point winner and runner-up in a bumper and a maiden hurdle, though was beaten 16l on that
latter occasion and inherited second place; brought down at the first last time; has to raise his
game against this opposition.
Buddy Holly 5 11-0 N Henderson Nico de Boinville 12-1 - 110 124
Looked to have a future when shaping well in an Irish bumper (good to yielding) and a C&D
novice (soft); Ffos Las last time was a backward step but heavy ground there doesn't suit all
horses; remains of interest.
Laurier Des Obeaux 5 11-0 G & J Moore Caoilin Quinn 20-1 - 91 116
Made an encouraging start over hurdles at Lingfield (2m3f, good to soft) and it was a better race
when beaten 18l here in December; should improve, but it's needed.
Mulinas 7 11-0 P Nicholls Sam Twiston-Davies 33-1 - 32 94
Beat Potters Charm in an Irish point; two bumper runs were okay but he has struggled in two
maiden hurdles following a long absence; looks the clear stable second string.
SPOTLIGHT VERDICT Irish raider The Big Clubman brings Graded form and it's clear that he failed to give his true
running last time. However, TALK TO THE MAN posted an eyecatching RPR when winning as he liked at Taunton and this
scopey 6yo possesses considerable potential. Buddy Holly had shaped well before getting stuck in the mud at Ffos
Las.[Alistair Jones]

Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR
Kotmask 8 12-0p G & J Moore Caoilin Quinn 8-1 129 129 137
Resurgent in first-time blinkers when second to an improver at Sandown in January (good; fine
on soft) and fell midrace back there last time; it's surprising to see cheekpieces back on (beaten
10l in December when tried in them once before) but he has a big effort in him off this mark.
Hardy Du Seuil 9 11-11p J Snowden Isabelle Ryder (5) 9-2 126 110 134
Won over hurdles in November and has done well on his belated return to fences, following his
fourth at Haydock with a near miss at Carlisle (2m, good to soft); Isabelle Ryder again claims
her 5lb and this 9yo is up 3lb in future.
Daytime Dreaming 6 11-10 T Ellis Jack Andrews 15-8 125 109 133
Left clear when beating an exposed veteran at Southwell (2m, good to soft) but this 6yo hasn't
had much racing over hurdles or fences so he's probably on the upgrade; an 8lb rise might not
be the end of the world.
Pure Carbon 7 11-4 H Derham Brendan Powell 2-1 119 123 133
Two wins and a second to show from his completed starts over fences and he went up only 4lb
for the Musselburgh success a month ago (2m, good to soft); this is only his 11th career start,
so firmly in calculations.
Rath Gaul Hill 8 11-1tp S Drinkwater Sam Twiston-Davies 12-1 116 122 136
Returning from an absence when edging home in this 12 months ago off 2lb higher; his
penultimate effort (here in first-time cheekpieces) was respectable and it's perhaps best to
forget Sandown last time when his best form has been on left-handed tracks; respected.
First Angel 10 10-7 M Keighley Sean Bowen 8-1 108 125 131
Sean Bowen was also aboard when this 10yo made it 3-10 over fences at Taunton 13 months
ago (2m, good to soft) on second run back from 478 days off; he needed the first and that may
again be the case here, after 405 days off, but he's well handicapped.
SPOTLIGHT VERDICT Tricky, with none of the six dismissed with any confidence. DAYTIME DREAMING perhaps has
the most upside with him being so lightly raced and he's preferred over Pure Carbon who has hit the ground running over
fences. Last year's winner Rath Gaul Hill probably has to go left handed so his Sandown blip last time is readily
forgiven.[Alistair Jones]

Trainer Jockey SP OR TS RPR
Tiny Tetley 8 12-2 P Hobbs & J White Callum Pritchard (3) 16-1 132 128 131
Won four times over hurdles last season (2m7f-3m) but chasing didn't go to plan in the autumn
and he was soundly beaten when back over hurdles on Boxing Day; needs to get career back
on track.
Peacenik 7 11-13 K Price Gavin Sheehan 11-2 129 115 130
Low-mileage 7yo who left low-key seasonal debut behind when scoring by just over 5l at
Doncaster (2m3f, good to soft) in December and again ran well when placed here (2m4f, good)
later that month; open to improvement on first attempt at 3m; must be considered seriously.
Big City Roller 8 11-9p C Longsdon Lilly Pinchin 6-1 125 - -
2-3 over fences this season, with both wins gained in four-runner 2m4f races on heavy ground
(cheekpieces added last time); faces a different test on this return to hurdling but could have
untapped potential over 3m.
Benign Dictator 9 11-8p O Murphy Sean Bowen 8-1 124 125 133
3-15 over hurdles, latest win at Warwick (3m2f, good to soft) on New Year's Eve; below form on
latest outing, though, and needs to bounce back with career-best effort here; cheekpieces
(absent this term) are refitted.
Magical King 7 11-6p S Edmunds Charlie Hammond 20-1 122 - 131
Consistent over hurdles last season, with best effort a C&D second (soft) just over a year ago;
disappointing over fences this term (three attempts; blinkers tried last time) and this switch back
to hurdling needs to rekindle his enthusiasm; usual cheekpieces back on today.
Champagne Twist 8 11-4p B Pauling Elliott England (7) 25-1 120 - -
Very promising novice during 2023-24 season but generally very disappointing over last two
campaigns; pulled up on last three chase/hurdle runs (cheekpieces added last time); big leap of
faith required to support him.
Jalisco Star 8 11-3t Laura Horsfall Kevin Brogan 7-1 119 118 130
2-4 since returned to hurdling in the autumn, the latter win gained in four-runner mares' race at
Chepstow (2m7f, soft) a fortnight ago; evidently in very good nick but has quite a bit more on
her plate here.
Fierce Warrior 7 11-2 N Henderson Nico de Boinville 8-1 118 - 128
Made good start to chasing career in November, notably when winning at Doncaster (3m2f,
soft); ran as though something was amiss there in December but has been given a two-month
break and has possibilities if back on song for this hurdle return.
Kruger Park 8 11-2t P Nicholls Jay Tidball (5) 5-1 118 122 134
Good fourth over C&D (soft) in November and outstayed next-time-out winner Jalisco Star when
scoring at Fontwell (3m2f, good to soft) on Boxing Day; still on workable mark after latest 2lb
rise; likely contender again.
Call Me Legend 6 11-0 P Hobbs & J White Mr Jack Stenhouse (7) 11-4 116 126 132
Improving novice who bids to complete a hat-trick after handicap wins at Exeter (2m7f, good to
soft) and Wincanton (3m, heavy) this year; moves up in grade but still needs to taken very
seriously.
SPOTLIGHT VERDICT Call Me Legend (second choice) is respected in his bid for a third win in a row, while Kruger
Park was nudged up only 2lb for his hard-fought won over Jalisco Star at Fontwell and will be suited by the return to this
C&D. However, PEACENIK (nap) ended last year in good form at around 2m4f and could quite plausibly have untapped
potential over 3m.[Chris Wilson]
